G. Ashok vs B.Venu And Another on 3 December, 2025
 In The High Court For The State Of Telangana

At Hyderabad
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 M.A.C.M.A.No.619 of 2019
 Date: 03.12.2025
Between:
G. Ashok
 .....Appellant
 And
B. Venu and another
 ....Respondents
Judgment:

This appeal, under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is filed by the appellant-injured challenging the award dated 31.12.2012 passed in M.V.O.P.No.2070 of 2010 by the Chairman,
MACT-cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad (for short "the Tribunal"), whereby the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.46,000/- with interest @ 7.5%
per annum for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: MACT-cum-XIV Additional Chief Judge (FTC), City Civil Courts, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 22.07.2010 at about 06.00 P.M., the appellant along with his relative-Mallesham, was proceeding on a scooter towards a shop in Mulkampalli Village and when they reached the bus stop, a lorry bearing No.AP 07 TU 7575, driven in a rash and negligent manner from Jagadevpur side, hit their scooter from behind, due to which, both fell down on the ground.

It is stated that the said Mallesham succumbed to injuries on the spot and the appellant sustained fracture of shaft of the left humerus, fracture of the collar bone, chest injury, multiple abrasions and other injuries.
It is further stated that the appellant was initially shifted to the Government Area Hospital, Bhongir and later to Gandhi Hospital, Secunderabad.
A case in Crime No.31 of 2010 under Sections 304-A and 337 IPC was registered by Thurkapally Police Station against the lorry driver.
The appellant filed the aforesaid claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- on account of the injures received by him.
3. The respondent No.1-owner of the lorry remained ex parte.
The respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed a counter denying the manner of accident and contended that the claim was excessive.

sentences.text: On appreciation of the evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the lorry driver and that the crime vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and accordingly, awarded compensation of Rs.46,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum.
Seeking enhancement of the compensation, the appellant filed the present appeal.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that P.W.2- Orthopaedic Surgeon who treated the appellant, clearly deposed that the appellant suffered fracture of the shaft of left humerus with multiple abrasions, that implants were inserted, that removal of implants would require about Rs.25,000/-, and that the permanent partial disability was in the range of 15%-20%.
It is submitted that the Tribunal failed to consider disability and future medical expenses, thereby awarding inadequate compensation.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2- Insurance Company submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is just, reasonable and proportionate to the injuries actually proved, and thus prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
7. The finding of the Tribunal regarding the manner of accident has attained finality, as neither the owner nor insurer challenged the same.
8. Coming to the quantum of compensation, the Tribunal granted compensation under pain and suffering, transportation, extra nourishment, medical expenses and loss of earnings, totalling Rs.46,000/-.

However, from the medical evidence of P.W.2, it is clear that the appellant sustained major fracture injuries requiring ORIF, with permanent partial disability assessed at 15%-20%, and that he would need removal of implants at an approximate cost of Rs.25,000/-.
The Tribunal did not consider disability or future medical expenditure.

The nature of injuries, period of hospitalization,
the fracture of humerus and collar bone, and the long-term impact on functional capacity warrant a reasonable enhancement.
Having regard to the evidence

, an additional sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards future medical expenses, removal of implants, and the consequential pain, suffering and functional limitations is considered just and proper.

Thus the appellant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.1,46,000/-.
9.
In the result, this appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation from Rs.46,000/- to Rs.1,46,000/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
The rest of the terms and conditions imposed by the Tribunal shall remain unaltered.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, the miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE C.V.BHASKAR REDDY Date: 03.12.2025 Bw G. Ashok vs B.Venu And Another on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40655928/
